evidence: app/package.json:11 — @gracile/gracile ^0.11.0, exactly the current stable release (0.11.0, ~April 2026); no -next/prerelease builds
app/package.json:17 — vite ^8.0.0 (resolves to 8.3.5); Vite 8 stable only since 2026-03-12 (vite.dev/blog/announcing-vite8), the newest major
app/server.mjs:7 — @gracile/gracile/hono adapter, part of the current 0.11 server-handler/adapter surface, used for every request (central)
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:8-50 — defineRoute({handler, document, template}) is the framework's documented core route shape, not an experimental flag
grep app/src for 'experimental|unstable|preview|beta|canary' — zero matches; measured facts also show experimental: []
reach.rationale: No experimental, preview or canary APIs anywhere, but the app's central features all rest on recently-stable releases: Gracile 0.11.0 (~6 months old, and pre-1.0) and the Rolldown-based Vite 8 major (~7 months old). That's the 'recently-stable in central places' band.

evidence: app/server.mjs:1-16 — the newest surfaces (hono adapter, getClientBuildPath, dist/server/entrypoint.js contract) are confined to this single 16-line file, mirroring the official minimal-server-hono starter
app/vite.config.js:1-7 — Vite 8 exposure is confined to a 7-line config using only the documented gracile({output:'server'}) plugin option
app/src/client/interactions.ts:1-55 — client side is plain DOM scripting; no @gracile/client router, no @gracile-labs/islands or hmr add-ons to contain
app/src/document.ts:1-31 — the only framework-provided custom element, <route-template-outlet> (line 25), sits in the shared document wrapper, one place to change
containment.rationale: Nothing experimental to contain; even the newest pieces (Vite 8, the hono adapter) are isolated to one config file and one server entrypoint, so a framework or Vite major bump would touch at most two small files.

evidence: SPEC.md — the framework is mandated ('The framework you must use is named in your instructions'), so the Gracile 0.11 baseline is not novelty-seeking
app/server.mjs:9-14 — honoAdapter + serveStatic is the framework's own documented production-server recipe (official minimal-server-hono starter), not an exotic integration
app/vite.config.js:5 — output: 'server' is required for runtime SSR with request-time API fetching, which SPEC.md mandates (no build-time data embedding)
app/src/lib/api.ts:18-30 — data layer is plain fetch with in-memory caching, no experimental APIs
no usage of @gracile-labs/islands (marked 'Experimental' upstream) even though it would have tempted for the sortable tables — plain DOM handles them instead (app/src/client/interactions.ts:60-93)
justification.rationale: Every framework API used is either spec-mandated or the framework's own officially documented pattern for this exact setup; the app deliberately avoided the genuinely experimental add-ons despite the interactive filter/sort requirements.

findings.issue: Vite 8 (Rolldown-based) became stable only in March 2026; the app rides the newest major whose plugin/build ecosystem is still settling, though @gracile/engine 0.12 officially supports it (peer range vite ^7 || ^8).
findings.suggestion: Fine to keep, but record in the lockfile that Vite 7 is the fallback if a plugin or build regression appears; review the Vite migration guide notes when bumping.

findings.issue: Gracile is pre-1.0 (0.11.0, current stable but ~6 months old); under 0.x semver even minor releases can break APIs the app leans on (defineRoute shape, route-template-outlet, entrypoint.js contract).
findings.suggestion: Consider pinning an exact version instead of ^0.11.0, and upgrade Gracile minor releases deliberately with the changelog in hand.

findings.issue: The @gracile/gracile/hono adapter is one of the younger surfaces of the framework (server/handler adapter line revamped in the 0.10/0.11 era) and is the app's only request entrypoint.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable since it matches the official starter verbatim; just keep it in this single file so an adapter API change is a one-file fix.

summary: The app is conservative: zero experimental, preview or canary APIs, no unstable_* flags, and it deliberately skips Gracile's explicitly experimental add-ons (@gracile-labs/islands, client router) in favor of documented stable patterns copied from the official starter. Its only exposure to newness is riding the framework's current stable release (0.11.0, pre-1.0) and the recently-stable Vite 8 major. That risk is well contained in two small files (vite.config.js, server.mjs), so breakage from upstream churn would be cheap to absorb.
